# Psalm 77 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choir director: according to Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph. I cry out to God — out loud! I cry out to God and beg him to listen.

**2** When I was in deep trouble, I searched for the Lord. All night long I stretched out my hands in prayer, but nothing could comfort me.

**3** I think about God and groan. I try to meditate, but my spirit just gives out. Selah

**4** You kept my eyes wide open through the night; I was so distressed I couldn't even form words.

**5** I thought back to the old days, years long past.

**6** I remembered the songs I used to sing at night. I searched my heart, and my spirit demanded answers:

**7** "Has the Lord rejected us forever? Will he never show us his favor again?

**8** Has his faithful love dried up for good? Has his promise expired — permanently?

**9** Has God forgotten how to be kind? Has his anger slammed the door on his compassion?" Selah

**10** Then I said to myself, 'This is what tears me apart — has the Most High changed?'

**11** But I will remember what the LORD has done! Yes, I will remember the miracles you did long ago.

**12** I will think carefully about everything you've done and reflect on your mighty acts.

**13** God, everything you do is holy. What god can even compare with our God?

**14** You are the God who performs miracles; you showed the nations your incredible power.

**15** With your mighty arm you rescued your people — the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah

**16** The waters saw you, God — the waters saw you and shuddered! The ocean depths themselves trembled.

**17** The clouds dumped their rain; the sky crackled with thunder; your lightning bolts shot in every direction.

**18** Your thunder roared in the whirlwind; lightning flashes lit up the world; the earth shook and quaked.

**19** Your road ran right through the sea; your path cut through mighty waters — but no one could see your footprints.

**20** You led your people like a shepherd leads his flock, with Moses and Aaron guiding the way.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **77:7-9**: Six devastating questions in a row — each one worse than the last. Has God's love ended? His promises? His kindness? His compassion? This is what faith looks like in the dark.

- **77:19-20**: The ending is brilliant and unexpected. After all that cosmic power — thunder, lightning, trembling oceans — the psalm lands on the tender image of a shepherd leading his flock. God's power serves his gentleness.

— PNEUMA
